name: Relayed inner-discovery prior (design r), decided by an on-policy/off-policy, chain-replicated held-out test
core_idea: Move the recursion to where its data are cheap, and decide it once where claims are expensive. Design r is design q's representation search inside acquisition, run at train 200, where it gets about 20 program rounds instead of about 4, with one addition. For every program variant it tries, it records which edit cells produced the variant and how the variant ranked against the current programs on training problems. It writes those per-cell sums into the kernel's existing memory channel. At the start of the next acquisition (the next category) it sets its edit prior from everything recorded so far. So each discovered representation, and each failed one, changes how later representations are generated: on-policy, across categories, using only the learner's own totals on training problems. Whether this makes the learner a better discoverer is decided by one pre-registered comparison on the four fresh held-out categories. It is powered for an effect of about 0.007 and compares against: the same learner with no memory, with a cell-shuffled memory, and with an off-policy memory; a CPU-matched learner that does no discovery; and a ceiling arm with 4x the budget, which names the limit if the answer is negative.
why_it_beats_the_measured_limit:
THE MEASURED LIMIT (design o, outer recursion):
- The rule accepts only a mean of at least 0.0134 over 16 pairs (t >= 2.6 at the median confirmation sd 0.0206).
- Confirmed candidates were worth +0.0012 on unselected seeds (+0.0089 on the seeds that selected them); the correlation between screening and promotion values is 0.10.
- 0 of 29 steps were accepted. At the null rate of about 0.01 per step, a 6,000 CPU-s lineage expects about 0.1 acceptances, and almost all of them would be false.
- Confirming a true +0.005 with power 0.8 at paired sd 0.021 needs about 209 pairs (about 1,500 CPU-s). A true +0.0012 needs about 3,600 pairs.
- A powered swap test (16 pairs of 6,000 CPU-s lineages) would cost 192,000 CPU-s, and its final parents would almost all be generation 0.
- The channel itself is inert: a principle learns 43 edit weights from about 10 updates of 6 noisy values.
- So the outer recursion cannot be decided within 300,000 CPU-s.

THIS DESIGN:

(1) Data for the recursion are variant outcomes inside acquisition.
- One variant scored on a 4-problem batch costs about 4 constructions, about 0.03-0.05 CPU-s.
- A chain of 12 source acquisitions at train 200 costs about 470 CPU-s and yields about 1,900 scored variants (20 program rounds x 8 variants x 12).
- A design o lineage yields about 60 scored candidates per 6,000 CPU-s. That is about 400 times more meta-level data per CPU-second here. These data are on training problems, not fresh instances; the held-out test decides whether that matters.
- Expected inner acceptances: q measured 15 confirmed switches in 62 program rounds (0.24 per round) under the two-batch rule. That gives about 5 per acquisition and about 60 per chain.

(2) The claim has exactly one registered acceptance, on held-out categories, at equal meter budget.
- Untrained answers are identical in every arm, so delta-gain equals delta-acquired.
- Planning noise: the paired sd of q minus o at train 40 was measured at 0.020-0.022 over all categories and 0.029 over job shop and QAP. Planning values: sigma_pair = 0.03; chain-to-chain sd tau = 0.008.
- 32 chains x 4 categories x 4 seeds = 512 pairs gives SE = 0.0019.
- The final test (t >= 2.45 on 32 chain means, one-sided alpha = 0.01) accepts an observed mean of 0.0047 or more.
- Power is 0.18, 0.55, 0.88 and 1.00 at delta = 0.003, 0.005, 0.007 and 0.010. Power 0.9 is reached at delta = 0.0072 (0.0062 if sigma = 0.02, 0.0084 if sigma = 0.04).
- False acceptance is 0.01 for the primary, and the family-wise error over the gated secondaries is at most 0.01. The secondaries use 256 pairs (power 0.9 at 0.0088).
- A non-binding futility look at 16 chains (stop if t < 0.5) stops with probability 0.69 under the null and 0.02 at delta = 0.007.
- Fewer chains are worse when tau > 0 (16 chains x 8 seeds gives SE 0.0024). Meta-training is cheap, so the chains, not the seeds, carry the replication.

(3) Why train 200 rather than 40:
- o0's noise on a 12-pair mean falls from 0.015 to 0.006 for 3.9 times the CPU, about 1.6 times more precision per CPU-second.
- The inner search gets about 20 program rounds instead of about 4 (q's starvation).
- o0 is saturated there (5 times the budget buys +0.006), so the matched control cannot buy the effect with CPU.

(4) CPU: about 175,000 of 300,000 machine CPU-s. <scratch>/panel/work/decisive/power.py reproduces these numbers.

PLAINLY: the effect it can detect (about 0.007) is a third of generation 0's whole acquisition gain (+0.021), and nothing measured so far shows a meta-level effect that large. If the true effect is +0.002, the likely outcome (probability about 0.8) is a decisive negative: the one-sided 95% upper bound of relay minus frozen falls below 0.007, and the ceiling, Level-1 and inner diagnostics name its cause. A positive comes with probability of about 0.1. Observed means between about 0.004 and 0.0047 are reported as inconclusive.
recursion:
WHAT CHANGES: generation only.
- In every program round, each variant's normalised rank difference from the current programs on the round's batch, d in [-1, 1], is credited to the edit cells that made it (1/k each for k edits). A confirmed switch also records its cells.
- At the end of acquire, the per-cell count, sum and sum of squares are appended to memory as one entry. There are 18 inner cells: score and pick insert, delete, replace, mutop, mutarg, swap, term and cross, plus theta perturb and grow.
- The kernel hands the memory to the next acquire. There the prior is w_c = clip(beta * m_c / s, -2, 2), where m_c = S_c / (N_c + 20) and s is the pooled sd of d. Variants are then drawn with softmax(w).
- So each discovered representation, and each failed variant, changes the distribution from which later representations are generated, on later categories.
- The chain is on-policy: the variants the next update learns from were drawn by the prior that the earlier updates produced. The improved discoverer generates the data for its own next improvement.
- Only statistics from training problems and the learner's own totals enter the memory. No score, reference or fresh instance does.
- Evaluation (the two-batch switch rule and the held-back check) and acceptance (the held-out test) are fixed. The false-acceptance rate therefore stays the registered one, and any effect is attributable to generation.

CONTROLS THAT ISOLATE THE EFFECT:
- frozen: empty memory. This is the total effect of the learner's own discovery experience.
- shuffled: the relay memory with its 18 cell labels permuted by a registered derangement. Same weight values and concentration, no information. This separates information from peakedness.
- off-policy: the same 12 source acquisitions, on the same categories and seeds, each run with an empty memory, their entries concatenated. Same amount of data, but generated by the unimproved discoverer. This separates the recursive, on-policy component from mere accumulation. It is the test of the directive's 6.3 ("rather than merely accumulating ... memories") and of 'the improved mechanism provides an advantage in subsequent generations'.
- o0@matched and frozen@4B cover compute.

The memory holds no program and no constant, so no skill is carried. The directive's arm 3 therefore has nothing to separate, and arms 2 and 4 coincide with frozen.
mechanism_changes:
NEW: rsi6/learner/design_r.py (about 200 lines).
- class LearnerR(design_q.LearnerQ).
- The version record is design q's plus relay = {beta: 1.0, kappa: 20, cap: 2.0}, with validate, digest and differences. These values are fixed now and not tuned.
- _variant is overridden to also return the cells it applied; otherwise it is q's code.
- _acquire_open is q's loop plus logging of (cells, d) per variant and the cells of each confirmed switch.
- acquire reads the memory entries of kind 'r_stats', builds the prior with prior_from(entries, beta, kappa, cap), and adds it to the version's inner w for this acquisition (r0's own w is zeros). It then appends one 'r_stats' entry (N, S, Q, switches per cell, rounds, whether the capability keeps a switched program). Entries of other kinds pass through unchanged.
- permute_memory(memory, perm) builds the shuffled arm (driver only).
- Constants: CELLS = design_q.INNER_CELLS (18 cells), KIND = 'r_stats'.
- r0's inner settings are design q's generation 0, unchanged (share 0.5, 8 variants, edits 0.6/0.3/0.1, two-batch rule). With an empty memory, design r is design q exactly: same capability, answers and report counts (tested).

MODIFIED: rsi6/learner/designs.py.
- Adds dispatch for 'q' and 'r' (+8 lines).
- registration_o pins this file's hash. The edit therefore lands after the open experiment's restartable stages are recorded, or those stages are resumed from a checkout at their registered commit.

NEW: rsi6/open/relay.py (driver, about 260 lines, modelled on experiment_q.py).
- Stages 'meta' and 'heldout', with guard and registration checks.
- Records: r_memory (every chain step's memory, content and digest, because Cache returns no memory and run records keep only memory_in), r_matched, r_stage_done.

NEW: rsi6/open/relay_report.py (about 140 lines: endpoints, gate, diagnostics), rsi6/registry/registration_r.json, rsi6/tests/test_design_r.py (about 110 lines).

NOT CHANGED: rsi6/kernel/* (run, problem, environment, ledger, roles), the meter, the references, the adapters, design_o.py, design_q.py, edits.py, discovery*.py.
measurement_design:
ARMS
The first five arms use one version, r0, and differ only in the memory the kernel passes.
- relay: memory M_j of on-policy chain j.
- frozen: no memory (q with r0's settings).
- shuffled: pi_j(M_j).
- offpolicy: M'_j.
- o0@matched: design o generation 0, with its training budget raised pair by pair until its CPU reaches relay's (evaluate.raise_until, amendment 4 reading d).
- frozen@4B: frozen at train 800. A ceiling, deliberately not matched.
Untrained answers are identical in all arms (same programs, constants and apply stream), so the registered min(delta-acquired, delta-gain) equals delta-acquired.

META-TRAINING (registered; source categories only)
- 32 on-policy chains, each of 12 acquisitions at train 200, in a fixed order: job shop x3, QAP x3, p-median x3, knapsack x2, bin packing x1.
- Knapsack is used for its binary-choice structure. Its fresh scores carry no signal, but only its training-problem statistics enter the memory.
- Seeds: 250000 + 100j + k.
- The off-policy chains run the same (category, seed) list with empty memories.
- Partitioning and set covering are excluded for cost.

HELD-OUT
- Categories: single-machine weighted tardiness, UBQP, RCPSP, maximum clique. No learner runs on them before this stage. If fewer than three pass their audit, the stage waits.
- Budget: train 200, test_c 2, test_e 1, n_train 16, n_fresh 24.
- Size rule: if a category's predicted o0 CPU per run exceeds 60 s, its train budget is max(40, 200 * 60 / predicted). The prediction comes from the category's construction units via a CPU model fitted on source runs, and is fixed before any run.
- Seeds: 260000 + 10j + s, s = 0..3, per category.
- relay and frozen run on all 512 (category, chain, seed) pairs; shuffled, offpolicy and o0@matched on s in {0, 1} (256 pairs); frozen@4B on s = 0 (128 pairs).

ENDPOINTS
- E-R1 (primary): relay minus frozen, the unweighted mean over the four categories of each category's mean over its 128 pairs. One-sided t on the 32 chain means; reject at t >= 2.45 (alpha = 0.01).
- Non-binding futility look at 16 chains: if t < 0.5, the remaining relay, frozen, shuffled and offpolicy runs are not made; the diagnostic arms are completed.
- Then, in a fixed sequence: E-R2, relay minus shuffled > 0 (alpha 0.01). Then E-R3, relay minus o0@matched > 0, and E-R4, relay minus offpolicy > 0, by Holm at 0.01.
- If relay's CPU exceeds frozen's by more than 10% on a category, that category's E-R1 pairs use frozen@matched instead.
- Reported, not tested: the registered bootstrap (chains and seeds resampled, categories fixed, 5,000 draws), each category's sign, CPU ratios, and these diagnostics:
  - L1: frozen minus o0@matched (does inner discovery pay at equal CPU?).
  - L2: frozen@4B minus frozen (the most a generation prior that made inner search up to 4x more efficient could buy).
  - L3: inner productivity on held-out training problems (mean d per variant, switch rate, share of acquisitions keeping a switched program), from the run reports.
  - L4: correlation over the cells of per-cell means between source categories.
  - L5: shuffled minus frozen.

SUCCESS
- 'Improved its own ability to discover' requires E-R1 and E-R2.
- 'Recursively' additionally requires E-R4.
- 'Useful at matched compute' additionally requires E-R3.

WHAT A POSITIVE SHOWS: statistics of the learner's own discoveries, carried across categories, make its representation search produce more fresh-instance capability on four unseen categories, beyond an equally peaked uninformed prior.

WHAT A POSITIVE DOES NOT SHOW:
- discovery of learning principles (the theta-learning programs are not searched inside acquisition);
- open-ended or multi-level recursion (the update rule is human-written);
- verification of each of the 12 generations (only the end of the chain is verified);
- self-discovered cells or instructions;
- anything beyond these four categories (fixed-effect inference);
- anything at train 40.

WHAT A NEGATIVE ESTABLISHES (E-R1's 95% upper bound below 0.007): in this regime, the learner's own discovery experience does not move acquisition on new categories by a third of generation 0's gain. The limit is named by the diagnostics:
- L2 < 0.004: an object-level ceiling, so no generation prior can matter.
- L2 >= 0.007 but no L3 gain: discovery knowledge does not transfer (meta-level analogue of fact 1; see L4).
- An L3 gain without an acquired gain: inner discoveries overfit training problems.
- L1 < 0: inner discovery is harmful at equal CPU.
Observed means between the two bounds are reported as inconclusive.

FAMILY-WISE RISK
- Within the experiment: at most 0.01 (the gate). The futility look spends no alpha.
- Across attempts: trying techniques until one passes at 0.05 gives a false-success probability of 1 - 0.95^K: 0.23 after 5 attempts, 0.40 after 10.
- Inside design o alone, at 0.08 to 0.13 false acceptance per lineage over its eight distinct lineages, at least one false acceptance has probability about 0.5 to 0.6.
- This registration therefore also registers an alpha-spending rule: 0.05 in total over all further registered success claims; 0.01 spent here; at most 0.01 per later attempt, each on categories no earlier attempt evaluated on (the four fresh categories are consumed here).
- A success counts as established only after replication on an independent set at 0.05 (the sealed targets after their test, or new categories). That bounds a false established claim at about 0.0005.
predictions: R-P1 (meta-training): in at least 24 of 32 on-policy chains, at least two of score/replace, score/mutop and score/swap are among the three lowest prior weights after 12 acquisitions. Expected: 28 of 32.
R-P2 (L4, source): the mean over pairs of source categories of the Spearman correlation of per-cell mean d over the 18 cells is at least 0.4. Expected: 0.5, carried mostly by the destructive cells.
R-P3 (L3, held-out): relay's mean d per variant exceeds frozen's on all four held-out categories, and its confirmed-switch rate per program round is at least 20% higher (relative). Expected: +30%.
R-P4 (L1): frozen minus o0@matched on held-out = -0.003 (90% predictive interval -0.012 to +0.006); not positive.
R-P6 (E-R1): relay minus frozen = +0.002 (interval -0.003 to +0.007). E-R1 not met. The decisive negative (95% upper bound below 0.007) has probability about 0.8; E-R1 met has probability about 0.1.
R-P7: relay minus shuffled = +0.004 (the shuffled prior up-weights destructive cells); relay minus offpolicy = 0.000 (absolute value below 0.003); relay minus o0@matched = -0.001.
R-P8: relay/frozen CPU ratio between 0.95 and 1.10 on every held-out category.
R-P9: at the futility look (16 chains), the primary's t is below 0.5, with probability about 0.4.
failure_modes: Object-level ceiling: at train 200 the inner representation search does not turn more search into fresh-instance capability (L2 about 0, as o0's +0.006 for 5x budget suggests). No generation prior can then reach 0.007, and the experiment can only return a negative: informative, but it places the limit below the discoverer.

Category-specific discovery knowledge: per-cell statistics agree across source categories only through the destructive cells. On the held-out categories (two binary-choice, two scheduling) the prior removes waste but points nowhere useful.

Overfitting inside acquisition: the prior raises switch rates judged on 4-problem batches of training problems, but the switched programs do not generalise to fresh groups. L3 rises while acquired stays flat or falls.

On-policy blind spot: down-weighted destructive cells are rarely tried again, their shrunk means drift toward zero, and the prior oscillates. Off-policy may then beat relay (E-R4 negative). That is a finding against the recursion, not a defect of the test.
Peakedness artefact: any concentrated prior changes diversity regardless of what it encodes. Diagnosed by L5 and E-R2.
Compute confound: the learned prior favours edits that lengthen programs or read more sensors, so CPU differs at equal meter budget. Handled by the 1.10 ratio rule and reported.

Fresh categories costlier than the assumed 39 s per run at train 200: the size rule lowers their budget, starving inner search there and diluting the mean, or the reserve runs out and the interim result becomes final.
Chain variance above plan (tau > 0.012): power at 0.007 falls below 0.8. delta_min is recomputed from development, never after registration.
Inapplicable cells: pick edits are no-ops on ordered problems, and many sensors are degenerate with two options, so part of the prior's mass cannot act.
The training split does not depend on the seed, so a chain's three acquisitions on one category see the same 16 problems relabelled. The memory is narrower than 12 acquisitions suggest.
Scheduling: designs.py is pinned by registration_o. Editing it before the open experiment's restartable stages are recorded makes that driver refuse on resume.
Sequence risk: a pass at 0.01 that is not replicated on an independent set still carries the family-wise risk of all the attempts before it.
implementation_plan:
1. Code and tests first (about half a day): design_r.py (about 200 lines) and test_design_r.py (about 110 lines, on the synthetic fixtures of test_design_q.py). The tests check:
- an empty memory gives exactly design q's capability, answers and report counts;
- foreign memory entries pass through unchanged;
- the prior depends only on r_stats entries;
- permuting the memory's cell labels permutes w exactly;
- the meter is respected;
- runs repeat exactly.

2. designs.py dispatch for q and r (+8 lines), scheduled after the open experiment's restartable stages, or with those stages resumed from their registered commit.

3. relay.py and relay_report.py (about 400 lines, modelled on experiment_q.py; about half a day).
- r_memory records, so a resumed driver replays chains without recomputing.
- --dev writes a scratch ledger and refuses non-source categories.

4. Development on source categories only: scratch ledger, seeds from 9101 on, disjoint from the registered ones. Nothing is tuned: beta = 1, kappa = 20, cap = 2 and q's inner settings are fixed now.
- D1 (about 4,400 CPU-s): r0 and o0 at train 200, o0@matched, and r0 at 800 on job shop, QAP and p-median, 6 seeds each. Gives Level 1, the ceiling, sigma_pair at 200 and the CPU ratio. If r0/o0 CPU exceeds 1.25, cache compiled programs before going on.
- D2 (about 9,000): leave-one-source-category-out relay with 8 chains, testing relay, frozen and shuffled on job shop, QAP and p-median in turn, 2 seeds each. Gives tau_chain, sigma_pair(relay - frozen), a development estimate of the effect, and a check that no cell sits at the cap in more than half the chains.
- D3 (no CPU): L4 from D2's chains.
- D4 (about 1,000): the CPU model a + b * train * units from source records, which sets the held-out size rule.

5. Recompute delta_min and the predictions from D1 to D4. Write registration_r.json (arms, seeds, rules, predictions, the alpha-spending rule) and have it reviewed independently. Then register and run meta, then held-out: about 12 hours of the four cores.
compute_budget:
Machine CPU-seconds = recorded acquire+apply x 1.15, for the kernel's unrecorded scoring of training instances.

- Development (source categories only): about 16,200 (D1 about 5,000, D2 about 10,400, D4 about 1,200).
- Registered meta-training: about 33,800. That is 32 on-policy plus 32 off-policy chains x 12 acquisitions at train 200, about 469 s per chain, with the first acquisition of each chain shared.
- Registered held-out: about 124,900.
  - relay 512 + frozen 512 + shuffled 256 + offpolicy 256 runs at about 39 s: 68,900.
  - o0@matched, 256 pairs over about two levels: 34,400.
  - frozen@4B, 128 runs at about 147 s: 21,600.
- Total: about 174,900 of 300,000. The reserve of about 125,000 covers fresh categories costlier than assumed, and replays after a restart (served from the ledger).
- Under the null, the futility look saves about 24,000 in expectation.
- The held-out line scales with the unknown cost of the fresh categories. Assumed: 39 s per run at train 200, i.e. 27.5 s measured on job shop, p-median and QAP, x 1.41.
- Arithmetic: <scratch>/panel/work/decisive/power.py
